title: Tutor UX river map
status: Proposed framework; no human validation performed

nodes.quick: The logical goal: capability the child can use without solution help.
nodes.why: Keeps usability, learning and healthy return aligned.
nodes.relates: Receives the learner, experience and evidence branches.
nodes.deep: Measure interface independence and learning independence separately; preserve a voluntary stopping point.
nodes.example: Solve a fresh task next week.

nodes.quick: Understand the people and conditions the tutor must serve.
nodes.why: Prevents a polished experience for the wrong user.
nodes.relates: Groups learner fit, motivation and trust.
nodes.deep: Use observed needs and explicit preferences; age alone cannot define reading or subject ability.
nodes.example: A strong reader who needs larger controls.

nodes.quick: Match presentation and tasks to the actual learner.
nodes.why: Reduces avoidable effort before teaching starts.
nodes.relates: Combines age bands, access needs and contexts.
nodes.deep: Separate interface complexity, reading support and subject readiness.
nodes.example: Advanced math with spoken instructions.

nodes.quick: Initial presentation defaults for 5–7, 8–10 and 11–14.
nodes.why: A five-year-old and teenager need different presentation.
nodes.relates: Informs learner fit and the shared design system.
nodes.deep: Use the repo's bands, then permit support overrides without changing mastery rules.
nodes.example: Large tiles and Hear this for 5–7.

nodes.quick: Supports for seeing, hearing, reading, moving and communicating.
nodes.why: Allows a child to show knowledge through a usable interface.
nodes.relates: Directly informs multimodal input and usability tests.
nodes.deep: Keep motion, speech and reading support independent; verify the assessed skill survives the accommodation.
nodes.example: Read a math prompt aloud.

nodes.quick: The setting, device, connectivity and adult availability.
nodes.why: An interface must work where learning actually occurs.
nodes.relates: Constrains setup, resume, input and recovery.
nodes.deep: Test phone, tablet, laptop, shared devices and interrupted use separately.
nodes.example: Homework on an iPad at the kitchen table.

nodes.quick: Reasons to begin, persist and return to learning.
nodes.why: Engagement should support growing capability.
nodes.relates: Combines agency, competence and belonging.
nodes.deep: Look for voluntary return and meaningful work; minutes alone are ambiguous.
nodes.example: Return to finish a personally chosen build.

nodes.quick: Meaningful control over choices, help and stopping.
nodes.why: Protects ownership and prevents pressure to continue.
nodes.relates: Guides workflow contracts and the finish screen.
nodes.deep: Offer bounded choices; keep pause and stop available without lost progress.
nodes.example: Choose an example or finish for today.

nodes.quick: A visible sense of growing ability.
nodes.why: Makes progress satisfying for a useful reason.
nodes.relates: Connects motivation with feedback and independent mastery.
nodes.deep: Celebrate an observed strategy or demonstrated skill; avoid empty praise and automatic mastery rewards.
nodes.example: You checked the pieces were equal.

nodes.quick: Feeling welcomed, respected and able to ask for help.
nodes.why: Supports participation without shame or comparison.
nodes.relates: Shapes feedback, adult handoff and child protection.
nodes.deep: Use an inclusive tone and warm character without demanding loyalty or pretending emotional dependence.
nodes.example: Let's try a different way.

nodes.quick: Understandable protection, control and truthful claims.
nodes.why: Families need confidence that matches actual behavior.
nodes.relates: Groups child protection, adult control and honest AI.
nodes.deep: Show who can see work, what is saved and how errors are challenged.
nodes.example: A parent can inspect an uncertain grade.
nodes.eli5: Know what you can rely on.

nodes.quick: Boundaries for content, privacy, data use and wellbeing.
nodes.why: Avoids harm within ordinary learning workflows.
nodes.relates: Constrains setup, input, release gates and retention of data.
nodes.deep: Use age-appropriate notices, limited data and a reachable human help route; verify actual deployment duties.
nodes.example: Camera permission appears only when needed.

nodes.quick: Appropriate authority over setup, plans and private settings.
nodes.why: Lets adults guide learning while the child works independently.
nodes.relates: Connects setup, parent review, workflow contracts and trust.
nodes.deep: Require explicit Apply for proposed plan changes; maintain locking, review, export, deletion and undo.
nodes.example: Preview the revised plan before Apply.
nodes.eli5: A grown-up manages the important settings.

nodes.quick: AI identity, limits and uncertainty are understandable.
nodes.why: Prevents overtrust and misleading learning claims.
nodes.relates: Sets conditions for release gates and calibrated feedback.
nodes.deep: A model's confidence is not validated accuracy; preserve pending and disputed judgments.
nodes.example: I'm still checking this answer.

nodes.quick: Turn learning goals into a clear usable journey.
nodes.why: Connects the interface to the teaching process.
nodes.relates: Groups entry, the learning loop and interface behavior.
nodes.deep: Design state transitions and recovery, not only attractive screenshots.
nodes.example: Continue a mission after an interruption.

nodes.quick: A clear path from arriving to useful work.
nodes.why: A difficult start can prevent any learning.
nodes.relates: Combines setup, next action and resume.
nodes.deep: Give adults progressive setup and children an immediately understandable mission.
nodes.example: Start the saved fractions mission.

nodes.quick: Prepare access, consent, preferences and usable capabilities.
nodes.why: Avoids asking children to solve account or provider problems.
nodes.relates: Depends on adult control and current capability state.
nodes.deep: Keep AI-optional behavior truthful; provide a working path after Skip for now.
nodes.example: Show verified available activities, or ask the parent to finish setup.

nodes.quick: The single most useful action for the current state.
nodes.why: Reduces navigation decisions and makes progress clear.
nodes.relates: Uses learner evidence, contexts and workflow contracts.
nodes.deep: Promote Continue or one mission; keep homework and exploration available as secondary routes.
nodes.example: Let's go: compare two fractions.
nodes.eli5: Here is what to do next.

nodes.quick: Return to saved work with enough context to continue.
nodes.why: Makes interruption a recoverable event.
nodes.relates: Connects entry, recovery, saved drafts and retention.
nodes.deep: Preserve the exact step and relevant draft; show what was saved and what is still pending.
nodes.example: You're on step three; your question is saved.

nodes.quick: Attempt, receive teaching, and demonstrate what holds.
nodes.why: Organizes interactions around capability growth.
nodes.relates: Combines scaffold, feedback and independent mastery.
nodes.deep: Adapt to evidence; a short session may save a later check instead of rushing every stage.
nodes.example: Example, partial problem, fresh problem.

nodes.quick: Temporary support that helps a learner make the next step.
nodes.why: Teaches a principle while allowing later independence.
nodes.relates: Works with feedback and fades before independent evidence.
nodes.deep: Change representation or prerequisite when needed; repeated confusion does not prove useful effort.
nodes.example: A partly completed worked example.

nodes.quick: A specific response that helps the child understand their attempt.
nodes.why: Turns an answer into information for the next move.
nodes.relates: Feeds calibration and selects appropriate scaffolding.
nodes.deep: Distinguish input repair, genuine mistakes and uncertain grading; keep wording kind and concrete.
nodes.example: Check whether both pieces use the same whole.
nodes.eli5: A clue about your next move.

nodes.quick: Evidence under the engine's rules of unaided skill use.
nodes.why: Prevents coached completion from becoming a false learning claim.
nodes.relates: Must be checked later through retention and transfer.
nodes.deep: Preserve current eligibility, freshness, interleaving and across-session rules; one success is not broad mastery.
nodes.example: Several eligible fresh successes across days.
nodes.eli5: Show that the skill is yours.

nodes.quick: The controls, words, media and states people use.
nodes.why: Determines whether intentions become successful actions.
nodes.relates: Combines design system, multimodal input and recovery.
nodes.deep: Make one stable interaction structure work across ages, devices and worlds.
nodes.example: Same help control in every visual world.
nodes.eli5: The things you see and use.

nodes.quick: Reusable rules for components, words, layout and behavior.
nodes.why: Improves consistency and lets one fix help many screens.
nodes.relates: Expresses age, access, trust and workflow requirements.
nodes.deep: Specify focus, loading, errors, audio, motion and reading variants as well as colors.
nodes.example: One accessible answer component in six worlds.

nodes.quick: Appropriate ways to respond by tap, type, voice or paper.
nodes.why: Removes input barriers without changing the learning goal.
nodes.relates: Implements access needs and relies on recovery.
nodes.deep: Confirm uncertain capture; supply alternatives when the objective permits them; record construct-changing assistance.
nodes.example: Tap instead of dragging a fraction piece.
nodes.eli5: Choose a way to show your answer.

nodes.quick: Preserve work and explain a useful path after failure.
nodes.why: Protects trust and prevents technical errors becoming learning errors.
nodes.relates: Supports resume, input, feedback and workflow contracts.
nodes.deep: Keep drafts until acknowledgement; retries must not duplicate evidence or leak between learners.
nodes.example: Restore a question after a failed submission.
nodes.eli5: Fix the problem without starting over.

nodes.quick: Use evidence to decide what to keep or change.
nodes.why: Turns 'world class' into accountable work.
nodes.relates: Groups learning evidence, research and delivery.
nodes.deep: Keep implementation checks, child observations and efficacy evidence distinct.
nodes.example: Revise a confusing exit based on observed use.
nodes.eli5: Check it works and make it better.

nodes.quick: Records showing what the child can do and what remains uncertain.
nodes.why: Makes progress claims meaningful.
nodes.relates: Combines retention, transfer and calibration.
nodes.deep: Record objective, assistance, task demand, date and validity; untested is unknown.
nodes.example: A dated independent explanation with its task.

nodes.quick: Demonstrating a skill after a recorded delay.
nodes.why: Tests whether learning lasts beyond the session.
nodes.relates: Checks independent mastery and informs future review.
nodes.deep: Use reviewed fresh items at planned intervals; 7/28-day reporting is a product convention, not a universal optimum.
nodes.example: Solve an equivalent task seven days later.

nodes.quick: Using an idea in a meaningfully different situation.
nodes.why: Distinguishes flexible understanding from copying a pattern.
nodes.relates: Extends independent mastery and learning evidence.
nodes.deep: Specify near versus farther transfer and match the rubric to the actual objective.
nodes.example: Apply fractions to a new fair-sharing problem.

nodes.quick: How accurately a learner or system judges what is known.
nodes.why: Makes help and confidence more appropriate.
nodes.relates: Uses feedback and supports honest reporting.
nodes.deep: Track child confidence against comparable work and AI verdicts against independent human review separately.
nodes.example: Flag a confident but incorrect explanation.

nodes.quick: Direct inquiry into people, workflows and learning outcomes.
nodes.why: Challenges assumptions before scaling a design.
nodes.relates: Combines co-design, usability tests and field pilots.
nodes.deep: Recruit relevant groups; record consent/assent and separate observations from interpretations.
nodes.example: Watch a child recover from a wrong answer.
nodes.eli5: Learn from the people using it.

nodes.quick: Children and adults help explore and shape alternatives.
nodes.why: Finds needs adults designing alone may miss.
nodes.relates: Informs learner fit, motivation and prototypes.
nodes.deep: Use concrete activities and understandable choices; do not ask children to invent the whole system.
nodes.example: Children compare two ways to ask for help.

nodes.quick: Observe whether intended users complete realistic tasks.
nodes.why: Finds navigation, wording and recovery problems.
nodes.relates: Checks interface independence and informs iteration.
nodes.deep: Observe before prompting; count navigation help separately from teaching help and access support.
nodes.example: Start, miss, get help, save, return, finish.

nodes.quick: Repeated use in real homes with planned outcome checks.
nodes.why: Reveals novelty effects, context failures and learning gaps.
nodes.relates: Supplies evidence for iteration and controlled release.
nodes.deep: Use comparable tasks, later checks and a stated study plan; small pilots cannot prove universal effectiveness.
nodes.example: Several weeks of family use plus delayed checks.

nodes.quick: The repeatable process that carries a design into operation.
nodes.why: Keeps teams and agents aligned through release.
nodes.relates: Combines workflow contracts, release gates and iteration.
nodes.deep: Use one accountable owner, concrete artifacts and an independent evidence review per change.
nodes.example: One complete workflow improved in a small release.
nodes.eli5: Turn the plan into reliable work.

nodes.quick: Explicit rules for states, actions, evidence and failure paths.
nodes.why: Prevents happy-path screens with undefined behavior.
nodes.relates: Expresses agency and connects design to implementation.
nodes.deep: Specify entry, primary action, ownership, help, save, timeout, retry, exit and evidence effects.
nodes.example: A pending grade cannot become a failure.

nodes.quick: Evidence conditions that must hold before wider release.
nodes.why: Stops severe failures from being hidden by an average score.
nodes.relates: Enforces honest AI, access, recovery and learning rules.
nodes.deep: Use pass, fail, conditional or unknown with evidence; blocking defects cannot be averaged away.
nodes.example: Pause release for false mastery or lost work.

nodes.quick: A repeated, measured decision to keep, revise or stop a change.
nodes.why: Improves the product without endless feature sprawl.
nodes.relates: Uses field pilots, usability findings and release gates.
nodes.deep: Fix one important failure; define success beforehand; compare at the same learning objective.
nodes.example: Keep a clearer hint only if use and learning hold.
nodes.eli5: Make one useful improvement at a time.

cross_links.label: informs
cross_links.why: Access needs determine which input alternatives and accommodations must be usable.

cross_links.label: constrains
cross_links.why: Agency requires workflow contracts to preserve choice, help, pause and stopping.

cross_links.label: informs
cross_links.why: Feedback helps the child judge understanding and exposes uncertain judgments for review.

cross_links.label: checked later
cross_links.why: Independent mastery claims need later evidence of retention at an appropriate objective and demand.

cross_links.label: sets gates
cross_links.why: Honest AI requires release gates for truthful claims, uncertain judgments and usable challenge paths.

cross_links.label: guides
cross_links.why: Field pilots provide repeated-use evidence for decisions to keep, revise or stop a change.
